subject: common-workplace-fundamentals
summary: Explains the types of technical documentation, strategies for finding information efficiently, and how to handle outdated or incomplete docs.
key_points: Different document types serve different purposes — match your goal to the right type.
Use TOC navigation, search, and code examples to find information quickly.
When docs are outdated, source code and commit logs are the most reliable references.
misconceptions: You should read documentation from beginning to end.
Blog posts and Stack Overflow answers are more reliable than official docs.
If documentation is missing, guessing is the best approach.
check_questions: What are the main types of technical documentation and their purposes?
Why is it important to check the documentation version?
What is the most accurate information source when docs are outdated?

fact_candidates: Types of technical documentation and their purposes (README, API reference, tutorial, etc.)
Strategies for efficient documentation reading (TOC, search, code examples)
practical_judgment_candidates: Choosing the right type of documentation for a given task
Deciding what to do when official documentation is outdated
error_interpretation_candidates: Recognizing that an API call fails because the wrong documentation version was referenced
scenario_candidates: Integrating an external payment API using official docs
Discovering internal framework docs are outdated and inconsistent with code
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Prioritizing blog posts over official documentation
Skipping version verification when referencing documentation
